findings.who: An investor holds an international bond fund or a foreign-bond ETF. The fund's foreign income came from interest on foreign bonds and passed through as fund distributions. The fund reports it on Form 1099-DIV, with foreign tax withheld in box 7 and foreign source income on its year-end statement.
findings.why_no: The helper asks whether the column's foreign income is 'dividends, interest or both'. The filer knows the fund holds bonds and that the foreign income is foreign interest, so they choose 'interest'. That leaves has_div false, even though everything was paid to them as RIC dividends on a 1099-DIV.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 19, Tip: 'If foreign tax paid on passive income is reported to you in U.S. dollars on a Form 1099-DIV ... Enter "1099 taxes" in column (l) of Part II, and complete columns (q) through (u)'
findings.fix: Ask by document, not by economic character: 'Did any of this column's foreign income or foreign tax come from Form 1099-DIV, a fund's year-end statement, or dividends on foreign shares?' Add help: 'Fund distributions, including bond funds, are dividends here even if the fund earned interest.'

findings.who: A partner or LLC member gets a Schedule K-1 and K-3 from an investment partnership or hedge fund. The K-3 reports foreign-source dividends with foreign tax withheld at source. The filer also has foreign bank interest in the same country.
findings.why_no: The filer thinks of the amount as 'partnership income from a K-1', not as dividends they received. The helper's dividends, interest or both choice reads as asking what they personally received, so they pick 'interest' for the bank interest. The dividends and the tax withheld on them, passed through on the K-3, are dropped.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 11, Lines 1a and 1b: 'Include income in the category checked above Part I that is taxable by the United States and is from sources within the country entered on line i'
findings.fix: Broaden the helper's help: 'Count dividends you received directly and dividends passed through to you on Schedule K-1/K-3 from a partnership, S corporation, estate or trust (you or your spouse).'

findings.who: A filer's column for one country has foreign dividends together with other passive income, such as royalties, rents or gains on foreign shares. Or a filer received substitute payments in lieu of foreign dividends on loaned shares (Form 1099-MISC), with foreign tax withheld.
findings.why_no: Only three choices are offered: 'dividends, interest or both'. A column that is mostly royalties or rents with some dividends fits none of them, so the filer may pick 'interest' or stop at the closest wrong option. Substitute payments are not labeled 'dividends' on the filer's form.
findings.irs_text: f1116 p. 1, Part II: 'Taxes withheld at source on: (q) Dividends (r) Rents and royalties (s) Interest'
findings.fix: Replace the three-way choice with independent yes/no questions, one per column (q), (r) and (s): 'Was any foreign tax withheld on dividends (including fund distributions and payments in lieu of dividends)?' and so on. Offer an 'other or none' option so that no choice forces a wrong no.

findings.who: A married couple files jointly. The spouse alone holds foreign shares or a foreign-stock fund, with tax withheld, in a column that also has the filer's own foreign interest.
findings.why_no: The helper speaks of 'the column's foreign income' without saying 'you or your spouse'. The filer describes their own income, which is interest, and answers 'interest'.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 19, Tip: 'complete columns (q) through (u) for each foreign country indicated in Part I'
findings.fix: Word the helper as 'Did you or your spouse receive dividends from sources in this country (or from funds reporting foreign tax)?'

findings.who: A filer holds a foreign zero-coupon or deep-discount bond. The bond generates original issue discount, reported on Form 1099-OID or a foreign broker statement, or market discount, but pays no stated coupon.
findings.why_no: The helper offers only 'dividends, interest or both'. The filer thinks of OID or accrued discount as 'discount' or 'gain', not interest, so they pick 'dividends' or nothing. The help mentions only interest 'paid by a bank or company'.
findings.line: f1116col.int_income_if_int (and f1116col.tax_int_if_int if tax was withheld)
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 11, Lines 1a and 1b: "Include income in the category checked above Part I that is taxable by the United States and is from sources within the country entered on line i"
findings.fix: Ask whether the column's foreign income includes interest of any kind, including original issue discount (Form 1099-OID), discount on bonds, or interest credited but not withdrawn. Then classify.

findings.who: A partner in a partnership or an S corporation shareholder receives a Schedule K-1 and K-3 showing foreign-source passive interest and the foreign tax withheld on it. The filer has no Form 1099-INT.
findings.why_no: The filer sees the column's income as 'partnership income' or 'K-1 income', not as interest. The help points to 1099-INT box 6 and to bank or fund statements, so the filer does not classify the pass-through amount as interest.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 19, Tip: "reported to you in U.S. dollars on a Form 1099-DIV, 1099-INT, or similar statement ... complete columns (q) through (u) for each foreign country indicated in Part I"
findings.fix: In the helper question and help, name Schedule K-1/K-3 and other pass-through statements as sources of foreign interest and of foreign tax withheld on interest.

findings.who: A filer had foreign tax withheld this year on interest that was included in income in an earlier year. Examples are accrued interest or OID on a foreign bond that matured this year, or a foreign tax assessed this year after a foreign audit of an earlier year's interest. This year's column has little or no interest income.
findings.why_no: The filer reads the helper as asking about this year's income and truthfully says the column's income does not include interest. The withholding on interest (column (s)) is then forced to zero.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 19, Note: "If you are taking a credit for additional taxes paid or accrued as the result of an audit by a foreign taxing authority ... attach a statement to Form 1116 identifying these taxes."
findings.fix: Gate the tax question on either condition: the column has foreign interest income, or foreign tax was withheld or paid this year on interest from any year. Alternatively, ask about the tax separately from the income type.

findings.who: A joint filer whose spouse alone holds a foreign bank account or a foreign bond that pays interest with foreign tax withheld. The filer's own foreign income in the column is dividends only.
findings.why_no: If the helper question asks about 'your' foreign income, the filer answers 'dividends' and omits the spouse's interest.
findings.irs_text: i1116 p. 11, Lines 1a and 1b: "Include income in the category checked above Part I that is taxable by the United States and is from sources within the country entered on line i"
findings.fix: Word the helper as 'Does the foreign income in this column, yours or your spouse's, include dividends, interest, or both?'

findings.who: A filer earns interest on a foreign bank deposit and the foreign bank withholds tax. The filer receives no Form 1099-INT, only a foreign-language bank statement or nothing at all.
findings.why_no: The tax question's help points to 'box 6 of Form 1099-INT'. A filer whose type answer is anchored on 1099 forms may report the column as dividends only. A filer with no such form may treat the withheld tax as not applicable.
findings.irs_text: f1116 p. 1, Part II: "Taxes withheld at source on: ... (s) Interest" (In U.S. dollars)
findings.fix: Help: 'Include interest and foreign tax withheld from it even if you received no U.S. form. Use the foreign bank's statement and convert to U.S. dollars.'
